provenance.purpose: Reviewed public region descriptions reused by the AVES country and homepage explorer previews; refresh when the source descriptions change.

regions.name: Queensland
regions.description: Begin around Cairns and the Atherton Tablelands, where rainforest, crater lakes and open wetlands invite very different ways of watching birds.
regions.gateway: Cairns, with time based on the Atherton Tablelands

regions.name: New South Wales
regions.description: Look beyond the city to Royal National Park’s forest and coast, then inland to the woodland and wetlands of the Hawkesbury area.
regions.gateway: Sydney, with separate outings south and north-west

regions.name: Tasmania
regions.description: Start from Hobart and give Bruny Island room in your plans: quiet woodland, coastal heath and birds found nowhere beyond Tasmania.
regions.gateway: Hobart, then Kettering for the Bruny Island ferry

regions.name: Victoria
regions.description: Begin near Melbourne and Geelong, where Serendip Sanctuary brings grassland, woodland and changing wetlands into a compact landscape.
regions.gateway: Melbourne or Geelong, with Serendip near Lara

regions.name: South Australia
regions.description: Travel from Adelaide towards the Coorong for long lagoon views, pelicans and shorebirds shaped by changing water conditions.
regions.gateway: Adelaide, travelling towards Meningie and the Coorong

regions.name: Western Australia
regions.description: Start with Perth’s northern wetlands and Yanchep’s woodland, where western parrots and fairywrens give familiar habitats a different character.
regions.gateway: Perth, with outings north to Yanchep and Yellagonga

regions.name: Northern Territory
regions.description: Begin around Darwin’s wetlands, then allow time for Kakadu’s billabongs and floodplains, where water and season set the rhythm.
regions.gateway: Darwin, with separate time for Fogg Dam and Kakadu

regions.name: Australian Capital Territory
regions.description: Use Canberra as a base for quiet wetlands, Tidbinbilla’s sheltered habitats and the wetter forests of Namadgi.
regions.gateway: Canberra, with outings to Tidbinbilla and Namadgi

regions.name: Jervis Bay Territory
regions.description: Explore the separate Jervis Bay Territory through Booderee’s coastal forest and heath, with time for birds between the beach views.
regions.gateway: Sydney or Canberra, travelling by road to Jervis Bay
